title: Extend ONNX Frontend with `com.microsoft.Pad` operator
body:
## Context
Neural networks are graphs consisting of nodes called operators. Each operator corresponds to a mathematical function, usually described in framework's documentation or an AI standard, such as ONNX.

OpenVINO ONNX Frontend is a component responsible for working with ONNX graphs and requires implementation of different ONNX operators in order to use ONNX models.

This task requires extending OpenVINO ONNX Frontend with `com.microsoft.Pad` operator.

Necessary help will be provided by ONNX Fronted team.


## Operator specification
Operator details can be found in [official ONNX Runtime docs](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/main/docs/ContribOperators.md#com.microsoft.Pad).


## Todo list
1. Create `.hpp` and `.cpp` files for `com.microsoft.Pad` [here](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/tree/master/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/op)
2. Prepare an implementation of this operator in form of a function. It should be placed in [opset 1 namespace](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/op/unique.hpp#L13). You can use the implementation of standard [ONNX Pad operator](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/op/pad.cpp) as a reference
3. Register the function in [ops_bridge.cpp](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/ops_bridge.cpp#L554-L560) while keeping alphabetical order
4. Create test model(s) in [ONNX models directory](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/tree/master/src/frontends/onnx/tests/models/com.microsoft). OpenVINO test infrastructure then converts prototxt files to ONNX models - you will use those models later in tests
5. Add tests covering all use cases [here](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/tests/onnx_import_com_microsoft.in.cpp)

More details in [adding operators to ONNX Frontend guide](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/docs/how_to_add_op.md)


## Resources

- [Contribution guide - start here!](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Intel DevHub Discord channel](https://discord.gg/wPuqAujS) - engage in discussions, ask questions and talk to OpenVINO developers
- Guides on [ONNX Frontend architecture](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/docs/architecture.md) and [ONNX Frontend tests](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/docs/tests.md) are also available
- You can also see a [blog post on contributing to OpenVINO](https://medium.com/openvino-toolkit/how-to-contribute-to-an-ai-open-source-project-c741f48e009e)


## Example PRs
- https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/pull/15076
- https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/pull/14936
- https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/pull/12510


## Contact points
@participant2
@participant10
@reporter
Don't hesitate to reach out, we're here to help!

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant1 everything you described is correct, just a small comment from my side - the prototxt files that you need to create represent tiny, synthetic models that will later be used to test your implementation. You can look for existing models with the standard ONNX Pad operator, they can be found in OV's repository in ONNX FE tests.

Before the implementation please have a look at the spec https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/main/docs/ContribOperators.md#com.microsoft.Pad and compare it with the standard ONNX Pad op https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Operators.md#Pad Then you should be able to figure out if any part of the standard Pad implementation from OV could be reused to implement the one from the com.microsoft domain.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant3 thanks for taking a look! `com.microsoft.Pad` is an ONNX Runtime operator, specification of which can be found under https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/main/docs/ContribOperators.md#com.microsoft.Pad. 

This operator needs to be implemented (translated to OpenVINO code) on our side. There are three similar issues, because three different operators need implementation. I'd recommend to start by taking a look at the example PRs and the operator documentation.

> I mean where is the com.microsoft.Pad file ?

It doesn't exist in OpenVINO - it needs to be created, which is exactly the first point in the Todo list section.

A good starting point for tests is usually operator specification from the standard. I see that Microsoft hasn't given any examples in https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/main/docs/ContribOperators.md#com.microsoft.Pad, but I think some basic tests can be similar to for example:
- https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.pad.html
- https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Changelog.md#Pad-19
- https://<redacted-host>/api_docs/python/tf/pad

After that it would be good to look for edge cases and possible differences which make `com.microsoft.Pad` unique, they should be tested as well. I am not certain if/how many differences there are, but they have to be taken into account.
